newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS OPEN-UP FOUR-POINT LEAD AT TOP OF TABLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS OPEN-UP FOUR-POINT LEAD AT TOP OF TABLE.

text.p: Juventus strengthened their grip on Italy's league title race with a clinical 2-0 victory over Lazio at the Olympic stadium on Sunday that opened up a four-point gap at the top of Serie A.
The European champions had two goals disallowed for off-side but still won comprehensively with strikes in each half from Michele Padovano.
Juventus, with 33 points from 17 matches, have already secured the "Winter Championship" -- the accolade traditionally awarded to the team leading Serie A at its halfway stage.

In 64 Serie A tournaments to date, the winner of the "Winter Championship" has gone on to take the overall league title on 43 occasions -- and there was little evidence on Sunday to suggest Juventus will prove an exception to the rule.

Neither second-placed Sampdoria, who needed a controversial last minute goal to earn a point at Fiorentina, nor Inter, beaten in a home match with Bologna for the first time in 20 years, look capable of keeping pace with the league leaders.
Sampdoria, with 29 points, lie four points adrift of Juve with Inter five points off the pace.
With two-points in their last three matches and the injured Alen Boksic out for the next two months, Juventus had recently given heart to their challengers.
But against Lazio, coach Marcello Lippi compensated for the absent Boksic by playing Alessandro Del Piero as a winger and Padovano as a lone striker, hitting Lazio on the counter-attack.
Padovano had the ball in the net in the 16th minute but the goal was disallowed for off-side.
There was no doubting the validity of Padovano's 31st minute effort -- a curling shot after a pacey run down the right.
After the break, the irrepressible Padovano struck again, pouncing on a loose ball for his sixth goal of the season after Paolo Negro had blocked Atilio Lombardo's shot on the line.
At Florence, even Roberto Mancini seemed to think he was off-side when he nonchantly back-heeled the ball to Marco Franceschetti for Sampdoria's 89th minute equaliser.
But to Mancini's -- and Fiorentina's -- astonishment, the referee pointed to the half-way line and the visitors had saved their five-match unbeaten run after Gabriele Batistuta's 31st minute penalty.
On a snowy, winter's afternoon at the San Siro stadium, the ghosts of Inter's recent, inglorious past came back to haunt Roy Hodgson's side.
Three of the players dumped by the club following last season's poor performances -- Davide Fontolan, Andrea Seno and Russia's Igor Shalimov -- played key roles in Bologna's 2-0 win.
First, Fontolan laid on the cross from which Giancarlo Marocchi fired the visitors in front in the 38th minute.
Then, second-half substitute Shalimov rounded two players and goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca for the last-minute goal that gave Bologna their first victory since November 1996.
"Our championship ambitions remain intact," a resilient Hodgson told reporters after the match.
Cagliari threatened to spoil veteran defender Franco Baresi's 700th match for Milan until Roberto Baggio displayed a glimpse of his own golden past.
When Baggio was brought on as a second-half substitute, Milan were heading for their first defeat at Cagliari in 25 years thanks to Sandro Tovalieri's 44th-minute goal.
But in the 65th minute, Baggio somehow pulled a ball back from the by-line that Frenchman Christophe Dugarry transformed into his second goal in successive matches.
Despite the point, Baresi's Milan, sixth in the table, remain way below the standards the veteran defender has displayed throughout his 19-year career.

Fourth-placed Vicenza, fading after leading Serie A for the first time in their 94-history, raced into a two-goal lead at home to Napoli, Roberto Murgita and Uruguay's Marcelo Otero finding the net inside the opening 30 minutes.
But goals from French defender Alain Boghossian and Fabio Pecchia gave Napoli a point and left Vicenza level on 27 points with Parma.
Carlo Ancelotti's side pulled off their fourth successive win, a 1-0 victory over Verona, courtesy of Mario Stanic's 67th minute header.
Since the Croat joined Parma in December, the club are unbeaten in six matches.

Serie A's top scorer Filippo Inzaghi scored his 11th goal of the season in Atalanta's 1-0 victory over Reggiana, a result that puts Emilio Mondonico's shoestring side ahead of Carlos Bianchi's expensively assembled Roma, beaten 1-0 at Udinese.
